note: Anchor rules for the two heart hotspots that have no mesh part of their own.
Neither is separately addressable in BodyParts3D. The septum IS modelled —
since MRB-222 it is the interventricular portion of `Ventricular myocardium`
(FJ2428, isa tree) — but it is fused into that one element and cannot be
selected out of it, so the rule below still locates it from the two
ventricular cavities it lies between. No conducting tissue is modelled
anywhere in the dataset, so there is no sino-atrial node to select at all.
MRB-222 improved the septum anchor without changing this rule. The seam ray
now exits through the myocardium's epicardial surface, because there is one;
before, with the chambers modelled as bare blood casts, it exited through a
cavity cast's own skin. The dot therefore lands on real outer heart surface
at the anterior interventricular groove rather than on the surface of a
notional blood volume. The seam fit loosened from within 4% of the bounding
radius to a best of 5.9% at the same time, because the ventricle parts are
now cavity casts alone — the papillary lumps that used to bulk them out have
moved to the myocardium — so the two chamber surfaces converge less tightly.
The anchor still verifies: 26% out, seen from 18 of 36 views, framed view OK.
Each rule locates the structure from parts that DO exist. This is anatomy, so
it is written down and reviewable rather than derived from nothing — the
offsets are in units of the specimen's bounding radius, in the GLB's own
axes (+x patient's left, +y superior, +z anterior).
Every other hotspot takes its anchor from its own like-named mesh part and
needs no rule here.

anchors.why: The interventricular septum is the wall between the two ventricular cavities, so the midpoint of their centroids sits inside it. Its only honest EXTERNAL landmark is the anterior interventricular groove — the surface furrow running down the front of the heart directly over the septum, where the anterior interventricular branch of the left coronary artery runs, and the line a textbook diagram labels.
anchors.whySeam: Two earlier readings of 'the nearest exit' both missed the groove, and both were measured rather than argued. Choosing the most VISIBLE nearby surface walks out of the furrow and onto the neighbouring bulge: it put the dot antero-laterally on the left ventricle, 8.3% of the bounding radius from the right ventricle and 1.0% from the left — on a chamber wall, not on the wall between the chambers. Casting straight ANTERIORLY from between the two cavities is worse: it exits through the right ventricle's own free wall, because the right ventricle wraps around the front of the septum. The groove is neither. It is the seam where the two ventricular surfaces converge, so it is found as the surface point close to BOTH — on the anterior aspect, which is what distinguishes it from the posterior interventricular groove on the other side.

anchors.why: The sino-atrial node lies in the wall of the right atrium at the superior end, near where the superior vena cava enters. Offsetting the atrium's centroid superiorly and slightly anteriorly puts the anchor in that wall rather than in the middle of the chamber.
